methodological_rigor.justification: This ambispective multicenter cohort (17 centers in Spain/Italy; n=563 GEA; diagnosed 2019-2025) prespecifies biomarker definitions (CLDN18.2 high defined as 2+/3+ membrane staining in >=75% tumor cells using the VENTANA 43-14A assay, aligned with pivotal trials), uses appropriate descriptive comparisons (Wilcoxon, Fisher, chi-square), Kaplan-Meier survival estimates, and Cox proportional hazards for HR/95% CI with univariable and multivariable analyses. The pooled VHIO-300 NGS panel is ISO-15189 accredited. Weaknesses include local (rather than central) biomarker determination, substantial missingness (EBV missing 64.1%, PD-L1 missing 31.3%, NGS only 21.8%), small treatment subgroups (HER2-targeted n=46, anti-CLDN18.2 n=63), borderline/trend-level findings in the IO subgroup without multiplicity correction across the many cut-offs and combinations tested, and retrospective selection bias.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study addresses a timely, clinically actionable question of how CLDN18.2 overlaps with HER2, PD-L1, dMMR, EBV and how it modulates outcomes with chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, and immunotherapy in a post-SPOTLIGHT/GLOW landscape where zolbetuximab is now an option. Findings of 48.3% CLDN18.2-high prevalence (higher than prior reports), improved HER2-therapy outcomes in CLDN18.2-high tumors (HR 0.42 for PFS, P=0.03), and trend toward worse IO outcomes in CLDN18.2-high tumors directly inform treatment-selection dilemmas. Individual multicenter retrospective cohort design corresponds to Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is most applicable as this is a prognostic/predictive biomarker study in a GEA cohort. Reporting is solid for cohort description, biomarker definitions, assays, treatment subgroups, and survival analyses, with supplementary tables referenced extensively. Gaps against REMARK include no explicit pre-specified hypothesis framework for the many CLDN18.2 cut-off analyses, no sample-size/power justification, incomplete description of missing data handling, and no REMARK checklist. Data availability is limited: proprietary EHR and tissue data with no repository or code-sharing statement evident.

novelty_literature.justification: Multiple prior studies (Kubota, Hong, Waters, Qi, Malla, Arnold, Dottermusch, Jia, Pellino) have characterized CLDN18.2 prevalence and its interaction with other biomarkers, with some reporting worse IO outcomes in CLDN18.2-high tumors. The current contribution is a large European cohort, finding higher CLDN18.2 prevalence than in pivotal trials, corroborating Qi/Malla trend of poorer IO outcomes, and newly reporting improved HER2-targeted therapy outcomes in CLDN18.2-high tumors (an underexplored combination). Meaningful extension but not paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear structure with logical flow from cohort description through biomarker overlap, NGS, and treatment-specific outcomes. Tables and figures are appropriately detailed with standardized nomenclature. Discussion contextualizes findings against key literature (Qi, Malla, Kubota, Jia, Waters) and acknowledges limitations (retrospective, missingness, local assay, spatial heterogeneity). Minor issues include some dense tables combining multiple cut-offs and occasional redundancy in the highlights/abstract.

key_strengths: Large 17-center European ambispective GEA cohort (n=563) with standardized VENTANA 43-14A CLDN18.2 assessment aligned with SPOTLIGHT/GLOW pivotal trials
Systematic evaluation of CLDN18.2 overlap with HER2, PD-L1 CPS, MMR, and EBV alongside treatment-specific outcomes (chemotherapy, HER2-targeted, IO, anti-CLDN18.2)
Novel observation that CLDN18.2-high tumors derive greater benefit from HER2-targeted therapy (mPFS 17.0 vs 8.9 months, HR 0.42, P=0.03)
Corroborates the trend toward worse IO outcomes in CLDN18.2-high GEA (mOS 16.0 vs 43.0 months, HR 2.04, P=0.052), informing biomarker-driven first-line selection
key_concerns: Retrospective, ambispective design with substantial missingness (EBV 64.1% missing, PD-L1 31.3%, NGS 21.8%) limits biomarker-overlap precision
Local (not central) biomarker determination introduces inter-laboratory variability despite standardized antibody clone
Small HER2-targeted (n=46) and anti-CLDN18.2 (n=63) subgroups and many cut-off/combination analyses without multiplicity correction, producing borderline P-values (0.052, 0.07, 0.08)
No explicit REMARK adherence, no power justification, and no data/code availability statement
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically useful large European real-world cohort corroborating and extending prior CLDN18.2 biomarker-overlap findings, appropriate for a Tier 2 oncology journal such as ESMO Open or Annals of Oncology, capped below Tier 1 by retrospective design, missingness, and borderline statistical signals.
